DATE OF DECISION : 17" JANUARY, 2023 Devender .... Appellant Versus Parmod & another .... Respondents CORAM : HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE RAJBIR SEHRAWAT * OK OK OK Present: | Mr. Vivek Suri, Advocate for the appellant.

sentences.text:
Mr. Rajneesh Malhotra, Advocate for Ms. Mehar Khaneja, Advocate for respondent No.2-Insurance Co.
ek KO RAJBIR SEHRAWAT, J. (Oral)
CM-25213-CII-2015 This is application under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicle Act read with Section 5 of the Limitation Act for condonation of delay of 78 days in filing the present appeal.
Notice of the application was issued on 29.01.2016, however no reply has been filed by the opposite side so far.
For the reasons mentioned in the application, which is accompanied by affidavit, the application is allowed as prayed for and the delay of 78 days in filing the appeal is condoned.

The present appeal has been filed by the appellant-claimant against the award dated 29.04.2015 passed by the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Rohtak (for short, the Tribunal), whereby the claim petition of the appellant was dismissed.
2. For the purpose of the present appeal, the parties would be referred to as they were described in the original claim petition filed before the Tribunal.

Devender vs Parmod And Anr on 17 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/149458573/
1 3.

The brief facts, giving rise to the present appeal, are that the claimant-injured filed a claim petition alleging therein that on 10.03.2012 the petitioner was going on motorcycle bearing registration No. HR-26C- 9661 and Neeraj son of Jai Bhagwan was the pillion rider.

When they reached near Village Nanond turning; at village Kheri Sadh; at about 8.30pm; a Scorpio car bearing registration No.HR 12R-3377 driven by Parmod rashly, negligently and at a high speed came and struck against the motorcycle from behind.
Due to that impact Neeraj fell down and the petitioner was dragged to a considerable distance.
Neeraj succumbed to the injuries and the petitioner also sustained serious and grievous multiple injuries on his person.
He was taken to PGIMS Rohtak in unconscious state.
There he remained unconscious for long time and his jaws were stitched.
An FIR was lodged in the matter by father of Neeraj.
Due to this accident the petitioner had to incur expenditure of about 10 lacs on account of treatment, medicines, transportation and attendant charges etc.
He remained admitted in several hospitals and was operated upon.
As a result he claimed a compensation of 22,00,000/-.
4. The said claim petition has been dismissed by the Tribunal without even assessing the aspect of nature of injuries and disability or the quantum of expenses incurred by the petitioner.

The reason given by the Tribunal is that the incident involved in the case was caused with intention of causing murder, therefore, it is not a case of negligent driving on the road and hence the claim petition under the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 is not maintainable.
The counsel for the petitioner has submitted that the approach of the Tribunal is totally wrong.
The fact remains that the petitioner has received injuries in the road accident caused by the vehicle being driven by the respondent No.1.
Whatever be the reason or motive behind the accident the petitioner cannot be denied the compensation on account of loss suffered by him on account of accident.
Intention to commit murder is totally irrelevant for the purpose of the provisions of the Motor Vehicle Act.
The counsel has further submitted that, otherwise also, registration of a criminal case is not a sine qua non for maintaining the claim petition.
Hence, the Tribunal has travelled on a wrong trajectory in introducing the facts and other aspects of the criminal case into the claim proceedings just to deny compensation to the petitioner.
Hence, the order deserves to be set aside.
The Tribunal deserves to be directed to adjudicate the issue on merits involved in the claim petition.

The counsel for the petitioner has relied upon the judgment delivered by this Court in FAO No. 2558 of 2016 titled as Tata AIG General Insurance Company Limited Versus Surjeet Kaur and others decided on 7" March,
2022, to buttress his arguments.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 5. On the other hand, the counsel for the respondent-Insurance Company has submitted that the liability in a motor accident case is tortuous liability.
Therefore, unless there is a negligence involved in the accident, the claim petition under the Motor Vehicle Act is simply not maintainable.
Still further the counsel has submitted that intention to commit murder on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle, excludes the negligence per se.
Therefore, if it is a case of intentional murder, then no compensation can be claimed by the injured for the injuries suffered or death resulting in such a motor vehicle accident.

The counsel has relied upon one judgment rendered by the Supreme Court in the case of Surender Kumar Arora & anr. Vs. Dr. Manoj Bisla & ors. 2012 AIR (SC) 1918 and two judgments of this court in the cases of Manjit Kaur & another Vs. M/s. Mahak Cosmetics and Credit Private Limited and others, 214(67) RCR (Civil), 813 and National Insurance Company Lid Vs. Maya Devi & others, 2014339) RCR (Civil) 196.

2 6.
Having heard the counsel for the parties this court finds substance in the arguments raised by the counsel for the appellant.
It is not even in dispute that the respondent No.1-Parmod was driving the offending vehicle which smashed and caused accident to the different vehicle being driven by the appellant.
There is nothing in the Motor Vehicle Act to exclude the maintainability of the claim petition in such an accident.
Intention of the driver of the offending vehicle is totally immaterial for the purpose of claim petition.
The concept of Tort has no relevance in such an accident.
The liability to pay compensation is statutory liability and not the tortuous one.
This court has already held to this effect in Tata AIG General Insurance Co. Ltd. (supra) held that negligence is not the basis for award of compensation in a motor vehicle accident case.

entities.text: Tata AIG General Insurance Co. Ltd.
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Rather, the reason for entitling the family in distress to the compensation is the loss of earning family member.

It is also held in the said case that the family of a deceased is not granted compensation as a reward for carefully driving by the deceased earning member, rather, the compensation is awarded to compensate the loss resulting from such a motor vehicle accident.

Therefore, the argument of the counsel for the respondent-insurance company that even if the accident is deliberately caused, unless the accident involved negligence, the claim petition is not maintainable and sustainable per se is non-sustainable.
Needless to say that there is no provision in the Motor Vehicle Act which makes the negligence, per se, as basis for maintainability of the claim petition.

7. The argument that the intention to commit murder takes the incident of the accident out of the purview of the Motor Vehicle Act for the purpose of claim petition is not only non-sustainable but is an absurdity in logic.
If this argument is accepted and the claim petition is rejected on this ground then that would tantamount to giving premium to the person who caused accident on road; on his own conduct.
This is not the policy of the law or the philosophy of the law.
Moreover, even the intention to cause death by vehicle on road involved violations of rules prescribed for careful driving on road.
So the deliberate causing accident encompasses negligence within it for the purpose of motor vehicle accident.

The person causing accident on the road, resulting into death or injury to another person, is liable to compensate the family of the deceased or the injured person; irrespective of his intention in causing such an accident.
The judgments relied upon by counsel for the respondent-Insurance Company in this regard, are totally distinguishable on the facts.

The basic judgment on the issue, which is also mentioned in other judgments being relied upon by the counsel for the appellant is the judgment of the Supreme Court in the case of Rita Devi Vs. New India Assurance Co. Ltd. 2000 ACJ 801.

entities.text: Rita Devi Vs. New India Assurance Co. Ltd. 2000 ACJ 801
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: However, that judgment itself says that even if the intention to murder is there, then this would not per se exclude the liability to pay the compensation on account of having caused motor vehicle accident.
Liability would be relating to the facts of the individual case.
In that particular case; the facts were that vehicle involved in the accident was the auto-rickshaw owned and driven by the deceased himself in which the accused were travelling as passengers.
They tried to snatch that auto-rickshaw, which resulted in accident.
Therefore, the accused in that case were not driving any vehicle; as such, and hence it was not even a case of motor vehicle accident on the part of the respondents.
Rather, it was a case of snatching resulting into death.
Therefore, the liability on their part presumed to be excluded.
Therefore, the facts of that case have no parallel with the facts of the present case.
In fact, if the argument of the Insurance Company is accepted, then every claim petition can be defeated by asserting deliberate accident, irrespective of criminal consequences.

3 8.
Otherwise also this court has also held in FAO No.5296 of 2022 titled as United India Insurance Company Lid. Vs. Mamta & others

entities.text: United India Insurance Company Lid. Vs. Mamta & others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: decided on 06.01.2023 that even registration of criminal case is not a sine qua non for the maintainability of the claim petition and that the aspect of criminal case can, at the best, be used as a collateral aspect to the limited extent of corroborating assertion that accident had, in fact, taken place, and that beyond this; the aspects of criminal case are totally irrelevant for the purpose of decision of a claim petition.

The Tribunal is required to determine the claim of the claimant only on the basis of evidences led before it and not by getting swayed by the aspect of the criminal case, which might have been registered in the matter.
Needless to say that the claimants hardly have any say in the criminal case.
Police might not even be acting as per the statement or assertions made by the complainant in that case or may not even produce the appropriate person as witness in the criminal case.

9. Hence, this court is of the considered view that the Tribunal has gone totally wrong in rejecting the claim petition filed by the petitioner simply on the ground that there is a criminal case registered against the respondent No.1-driver of the offending vehicle, and in that case the intention of committing murder is alleged.

Even if the intention to commit murder is alleged against respondent No.1, that would not entitle him to avoid his liability to make the payment of compensation for the loss of life of another person or the injury suffered by another person.
The dichotomy of intention to murder and negligence for the purpose of claim petition is totally absurd and even defeats the object of the Act.
Therefore, the same cannot be sustained.
10. In view of the above, the award passed by the Tribunal is set aside.

The matter is remanded to the Tribunal for decision of the claim petition on merits; by appreciating the assertions made by the claimants before it, without getting affected by any aspect of the criminal case registered in the matter.
The parties are directed to appear before the Tribunal on 14.02.2023.
